stories.summary: CUSTODIAN authored and promoted a Memorial Court integration packet and its paired independent review to ready/automatic dispatch. The proposed scene would surround the existing Memorial Slab with verified paving, ring and wall art while preserving gameplay paths. No implementation landing or accepted review is established.

The production court, validation, independent review and host teardown remain unverified. Existing source constraints exclude the hash-mismatched full strip, forbid presenting a 256x128 wall as the planned 512x192 state, and leave footings pending approved art.

stories.headline: Field Scout playtest route clarified; finding and restoring the buggy still need proof
stories.summary: New CUSTODIAN documentation explains why the Field Scout does not appear in the default Awakening launch and how to enter its Contract sandbox. It also exposes unresolved gameplay gaps: the wreck may not be placed within reach, uses placeholder hover art, and charges raw resources instead of the approved fabricated assemblies. These are documented limitations, not new runtime fixes.
stories.body: Main commits 389df928 and 50f20cd9 update the current-state guide and Godot app README. The default F5 project run starts Awakening, which has no Field Scout; the authored wreck is in the Contract sandbox, entered through the explicit --custodian-start=contract-sandbox argument. F6 runs a selected scene rather than the project entrypoint. The vehicle loader seeks eligible parking, road or compound tiles but may leave the authored position when no candidate passes filtering. No fixed-seed reachability receipt was inspected. The wreck begins disabled, still renders hover compatibility frames, and uses a raw-resource recovery profile instead of the approved three fabricated assemblies. Existing recovery correction/review, Asset V2 vehicle family and vehicle-placement extraction packets own these gaps. Both new commits are documentation-only; no gameplay fix, independent review, canonical teardown or live host execution was established.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now explains how to find its first Field Scout buggy, and why players may still miss it. The vehicle belongs to a development-only Contract sandbox, not the default Awakening opening. New guidance also makes clear that spawning the wreck, seeing the right artwork and restoring it as designed are three different unfinished hurdles.

sections.heading: The right door into the sandbox
sections.text: The normal project launch opens Awakening, which has no Scout. An explicit Contract sandbox startup argument loads the scene containing the vehicle. The docs now distinguish Godot's F5 project run from F6's current-scene run, preventing a misleading playtest.

sections.heading: A vehicle can exist without being discoverable
sections.text: The generated world attempts to relocate the authored wreck to eligible parking, road or compound space. If no tile qualifies, its original scene position can remain. Existing smoke tests do not establish that a player can find the Scout at a fixed seed.

sections.heading: The wreck is not yet its final form
sections.text: The Scout starts disabled and uses placeholder hover art instead of its approved wheeled body. Its current repair recipe consumes raw resources rather than the three fabricated assemblies required by the approved restoration design. Separate queued workstreams own these changes.

insights.title: Scene presence is not a playable encounter
insights.explanation: A node in the Godot scene tree proves neither that it lands on reachable terrain nor that players can discover it. The next useful proof is a fixed-seed runtime placement and reachability test.

insights.title: Restoration and presentation are separate gates
insights.explanation: A working vehicle class does not establish the approved visual identity or resource economy. The Asset V2 family and recovery correction need their own implementation and review evidence.

article.takeaway: The playtest route is documented more accurately, but this is not a new gameplay implementation or accepted Scout release.
article.next_watch: Watch for a fixed-seed placement/reachability receipt, the fabricated-assembly recovery correction and canonical wheeled-body asset integration.

stories.headline: ChatGPT sender gains attachment safeguards, but live delivery remains untested
stories.summary: A new CUSTODIAN browser automation helper checks staged attachment names before sending and requires visible confirmation of a submitted message. Python syntax and CLI dry-run checks passed, but no real browser submission was tested. The change is landed code, not proof that messages or files can now be delivered reliably.
stories.body: Main commit 504658c3 introduces a ChatGPT sender helper that targets one existing conversation tab, refuses mismatched or unexpected attachments, and checks that a submitted message appears while the composer clears. Its --stage and --submit paths are opt-in. The author's validation record reports Python AST and CLI dry-run success, but explicitly says no live submit occurred. The browser composer and staged files were left unchanged. A missing send confirmation is treated as uncertain rather than permission to retry. No independent review, host execution, runtime liveness, or teardown was established.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's ChatGPT messaging helper now takes a more cautious approach to attachments and sending. It can recognize files already staged in the composer and refuse an unsafe mismatch, while a send attempt is not considered confirmed until the conversation visibly changes. The safeguard has landed in code, but actual delivery is still untested.

sections.heading: A safer handoff to the browser
sections.text: The helper targets one existing ChatGPT conversation and checks the exact attachment names already staged. It rejects unexpected files, duplicate requested names and conflicting drafts rather than replacing them silently.

sections.heading: Confirmation is not assumed
sections.text: After an explicitly requested send, the helper looks for the new user message and a cleared composer. If confirmation fails, it warns against automatic retries. The recorded checks were syntax and command-line dry runs, not a live browser submission.

insights.title: Uncertain sends should not become duplicate sends
insights.explanation: The new confirmation rule addresses an important failure mode in automation: clicking Send is not the same as knowing a message arrived. Refusing blind retries reduces the risk of repeated messages or attachments.

article.takeaway: The sender's safety logic is now present on main; real-world attachment and delivery behavior still needs a controlled test.
article.next_watch: A specifically authorized browser integration test should confirm staged files, one submission, and the resulting conversation state.

The floor/underlay and foreground/wall source roles have been corrected, with source identity checks specified. For the Crèche preparation and atomic room-console cutover only, the user approved direct gameplay-scale review rather than a paired Codex reviewer. Existing review packets were removed without a fabricated PASS. The clean-source and console packets remain draft/manual. The production room is still documented at 960×704; the 1464×1074 target has not been ingested or installed. Objective Asset V2 validation, geometry, navigation, route continuity, console FX and gameplay captures remain required. A Sepulcher memorial slab art packet also drops paired-review requirements but retains source verification and runtime gates. No host liveness, teardown, or full dispatcher inventory is established.

article.lead: The Awakening Crèche's art handoff has been corrected before installation: the approved floor and wall images now have their proper roles, and the final visual verdict will come from the user and ChatGPT rather than a paired Codex reviewer. The game itself has not changed.

sections.heading: A source mix-up resolved before cutover
sections.text: The updated packets identify separate approved 1464×1074 floor and foreground sources. Their previous labels were reversed. The documents explicitly preserve the existing 960×704 production room until source verification, registration and the scene cutover succeed.

sections.heading: Fewer review handoffs, not fewer quality gates
sections.text: The Crèche-specific paired reviewer packets were withdrawn, not passed. Direct review will assess actual gameplay-scale captures, while asset provenance, walkability, the route into the next room, and console activation effects still require objective validation.

sections.heading: The remaining work is in the game engine
sections.text: The clean-room plates must be durably staged and checked first. Only then can the floor, foreground, collision and independent console be switched together without leaving a broken or empty room.

insights.title: Correct art identity prevents a wrong-layer release
insights.explanation: A floor and foreground swap could break both visibility and collision assumptions. Recording their distinct identities before ingestion makes the eventual scene transaction safer.

insights.title: Review simplification is tightly scoped
insights.explanation: The direct-review exception applies only to Crèche source preparation and cutover. It does not certify runtime quality or remove unrelated Port review requirements.

article.takeaway: The art and review decisions are now documented, but the playable Crèche remains unchanged until a verified cutover.
article.next_watch: Look for durable source staging, Asset V2 receipts and real Godot gameplay captures showing the new room and its single console.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has pruned a set of stranded review and follow-up packets from its active planning queue. The cleanup makes the documented workload smaller, but it deliberately does not pretend the retired reviews passed or that their host resources were released.

sections.heading: A queue cleanup, not a code rollback
sections.text: The owner-directed commit deletes obsolete review and correction packet entries, including PixelPlanets follow-ups and the process ownership scanner hardening proposal. The commit states that landed runtime and archived implementation evidence remain preserved.

sections.heading: The host still needs separate accounting
sections.text: Removing a packet from Git does not prove its claimed review, execution lock, branch, or checkout was cleaned up. Those require exact-ref host evidence and separate authorization.

insights.title: Retired is not accepted
insights.explanation: Administrative retirement reduces active documentation without supplying a missing independent review receipt. Any downstream gate requiring an accepted PASS must still be assessed on its own evidence.

insights.title: The previous scanner plan is no longer an active packet

article.takeaway: The documented queue has been simplified, while runtime behavior and protected host disposition remain unverified.
article.next_watch: Watch for an independently evidenced disposition of any retained protected claims and for fresh, validated game or art milestones.

article.lead: A new implementation and independent-review pair targets a host-validation deadlock: a credential daemon with unreadable process directory was blocking ownership checks. The proposed fix must authenticate the service independently and continue rejecting spoofed or ambiguous processes. No scanner code changed.

sections.heading: A safety check meets an unusual host process
sections.text: The existing review ownership scan can stop on a same-user credential service before deciding whether it belongs to a reviewer. The packet proposes checking trustworthy process identity first, without accepting a process name alone.

sections.heading: The lock still matters
sections.text: The original protected review retains its claim and lock according to the packet. This documentation change neither frees that lock nor retries the review.

insights.title: Fail closed, even for the exception
insights.explanation: A genuine supervised credential daemon may be excluded only with independent identity proof. A forged name, unreadable identity, or possible review owner must remain blocking.

article.takeaway: The new source evidence establishes a defined next gate, not completed runtime or review acceptance.
article.next_watch: Owner: validate/promote the paired packet through normal authoring and resolve the existing protected lock before any claim.

sections.heading: The room grows on paper first
sections.text: The new source artwork is larger, but transparent margins must not become walkable space. Zone01 geometry, navigation and the north passage need measurement before the floor and foreground change together.

sections.heading: Original bytes, not a browser screenshot
sections.text: The follow-up source instruction prefers obtaining the original uploaded PNG via Chrome DevTools and verifying its SHA-256 before the Asset V2 ingest. If exact bytes cannot be obtained, the handoff must stop.

insights.title: The floor and walls are one cutover
insights.explanation: The plan prohibits deploying the larger floor against the old foreground. Both visual layers and the measured collision geometry must be validated together.

insights.title: Approval is not installation
